ResourcesPage.footer: More resources for developers and writers available at

repo.ai: Artificial intelligence tools, prompts, skills, and model configurations for the Xscriptor ecosystem.
repo.colors: All Xscriptor color palettes in one place — themes for terminals, editors, and IDEs.
repo.web: Web projects and UI components — Samurai security platform, Shinobi scraper, and the Xcomponents library.
repo.fresh: A collection of custom color themes for Fresh, the terminal text editor
repo.hyprland: A clean, performance-oriented Hyprland configuration featuring a [X] aesthetic, optimized for productivity and seamless workflow on X and Arch Linux
repo.jetbrains: Essential settings and customizations to improve accessibility and personalization of JetBrains IDEs using the Xscriptor ecosystem (themes, snippets...)
repo.obsidian: An elegant Obsidian theme for coders and writers with beautiful EB Garamond typography and flexible customization.
repo.opencode: An interactive CLI agent that helps with software engineering tasks directly from your terminal.
repo.vscode: A complete suite of customizations for VSCode & Forks, including themes, code snippets, and UI mods.
repo.x: Scripts for x, including the main x.sh entrypoint and modular add-ons. The base script installs the x wrapper, applies required system configuration after installation.
repo.xclock: A terminal-based clock application written in Rust, inspired by ttyclock. It features a digital clock with ASCII art, countdown timers, and various customization options.
repo.xfetch: A fast, lightweight, and highly customizable system information fetcher for the terminal, built in Rust. Display your system info with style and flexibility.
repo.xtop: Xtop, a modern, cross-platform TUI system monitor written in Rust. Inspired by btop, it leverages ratatui and sysinfo to provide real-time monitoring.
repo.xglass: A glassmorphism VS Code theme with translucent backgrounds and vibrant accents.
repo.oxt: Extended tooling and utilities for the Xscriptor development ecosystem.

JetBrainsPage.title: resources/
JetBrainsPage.description: A collection of 12 city-inspired themes for IntelliJ-based IDEs. Nine dark schemes and three light schemes, all built on the IntelliJ Platform 2025.3+ with Islands UI support.
JetBrainsPage.feature1: 12 city-inspired color schemes (9 dark, 3 light) across all IntelliJ-based IDEs
JetBrainsPage.feature2: Islands UI support for JetBrains IDEs 2025.3+ with full editor scheme integration
JetBrainsPage.feature3: Automated theme generation pipeline: edit colors.md, run generate_themes.py, deploy
JetBrainsPage.feature4: Comprehensive syntax highlighting for Java, Kotlin, Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, CSS, HTML, XML, Ruby, PHP, Go, Markdown, and RegExp
JetBrainsPage.feature5: Gradle-based build with IntelliJ Platform Plugin 2.x, Java 21 toolchain, and CI/CD integration
JetBrainsPage.themesDesc: All 12 schemes are organized around iconic cities, each with its own distinct color identity.
JetBrainsPage.installMarketplaceDesc: Open your IDE, go to Settings > Plugins > Marketplace, search for Xscriptor Theme, and click Install.
JetBrainsPage.installManualCmd: Download the plugin ZIP from GitHub releases and install via Settings > Plugins > Install Plugin from Disk.
JetBrainsPage.installBuildCmd:
git clone https://github.com/xscriptor/jetbrains
cd jetbrains/xscriptor-theme
./gradlew buildPlugin
JetBrainsPage.scriptsDesc: The repository ships with a Python script that parses colors.md and generates all 12 .theme.json files and .xml editor schemes automatically.
JetBrainsPage.scriptsExample:
# Generate all themes from colors.md
python3 scripts/generate_themes.py --output ./output

ObsidianPage.title: resources/
ObsidianPage.description: A refined literary-inspired theme for Obsidian, featuring EB Garamond typography and flexible customization for any workspace.

features.ebGaramond: Elegant EB Garamond typography with full italic and weight support
features.lightDark: Carefully tuned light and dark color palettes
features.codeBlocks: Enhanced code block readability with per-language backgrounds
features.styleSettings: Full Style Settings integration for real-time customization

ObsidianPage.installCommunityDesc: From Obsidian: Settings → Appearance → Community Themes → Search for Xscriptor and click Install.
ObsidianPage.installManualCmd: Copy the theme files into .obsidian/themes/Xscriptor/ and select it in Settings → Appearance
ObsidianPage.styleSettingsDesc: The theme integrates with the Style Settings plugin, giving you full control over transparency, colors, and typography.

settings.transparencyDesc: Control the transparency level of the application background.
settings.micaDesc: Enable a frosted glass blur effect over the workspace (requires translucent background).
settings.accentDesc: Customize the main accent color used across the theme.
settings.typographyDesc: Adjust base font size and line height for optimal readability.

ObsidianPage.devIntro: This theme ships with a Python automation toolkit that lets you generate your own custom Obsidian themes programmatically. The pipeline follows a declarative JSON-to-CSS workflow:
ObsidianPage.devQuickPaletteDesc: From just 8 color values and 4 background tones, the quick palette engine auto-derives approximately 150 CSS variables covering surfaces, borders, hovers, focus rings, callouts, tags, code blocks, and syntax tokens for both light and dark modes.
ObsidianPage.devFastPaletteDesc: Define just 2 emphasis colors and the script computes the full heading hierarchy (h1–h6), italic, muted, and faint tones automatically using configurable strength ratios.

WindowsPage.title: Taking windows to
WindowsPage.description: Complete collection of Xscriptor customizations for Windows 11: status bars (YASB, Zebar), taskbar themes, PowerShell tooling and more — all with the Xscriptor palette ecosystem.
WindowsPage.structureDesc: Everything is organized around three toolchains, each with one variant per palette:
WindowsPage.structYasbDesc: YASB theme pack — single source layout (config.yaml, themes/, theme switcher, deploy.ps1, generate.py) plus the archived per-theme folders in yasb/splited/.
WindowsPage.structZebarDesc: Zebar widget packs — neumorphism/ (soft-UI neumorphic bar with popups and 12 switchable palettes) and xneon/ (liquid-glass backup), with deploy.ps1 and generate-palettes.py.
WindowsPage.structWindhawkDesc: Windhawk taskbar themes (Taskbar Styler JSON) — three layouts: dock/ (floating centered dock), islands/ (floating rounded islands), translucid/ (legacy transparent); each with one variant per palette (x.json, madrid.json, …) and its own accent color.
WindowsPage.themesDesc: Every layout ships with the 12 city palettes, each with its own color identity.
WindowsPage.installRemote: Remote one-liners (Windows 11, PowerShell 5.1+, no git needed) — install the app if missing and deploy the theme packs from the repo:
WindowsPage.installCloneCmdYasb: powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File yasb\deploy.ps1   # YASB (winget install AmN.yasb)
WindowsPage.installCloneCmdZebar: powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File zebar\deploy.ps1  # Zebar (winget install glzr-io.zebar)
WindowsPage.installNote: Then enable the packs from the Zebar tray icon → My widgets.
WindowsPage.usageZebarDesc: One neumorphic island per indicator (system, media, disk, clock, CPU, memory, traffic, volume, battery, theme). Click any island for its detail popup (calendar, controls, usage charts); click the paintbrush to cycle the 12 palettes across every widget; click volume to mute.
WindowsPage.usageYasbDesc: Floating neumorphic islands; the theme_switcher button cycles the 12 theme stylesheets (left = next, right = previous).
WindowsPage.compat2: Requires the Hack Nerd Font (or any Nerd Font) for icon glyphs

FreshPage.title: resources/
FreshPage.description: Custom color themes for Fresh, the terminal text editor — a complete collection of JSON theme files, all with the Xscriptor palette ecosystem.
FreshPage.overviewDesc: This repository contains multiple JSON theme files compatible with Fresh. Install them into ~/.config/fresh/themes.
FreshPage.installRemote: Run the installer remotely with either curl or wget:
FreshPage.installNote: The installer creates ~/.config/fresh/themes if it does not exist and copies all themes there.
FreshPage.uninstallNote: This removes the themes provided by this repository. If the directory becomes empty, it is removed.
FreshPage.themesDesc: All 12 city palettes, ready to drop into Fresh.
FreshPage.note1: Fresh should read themes from ~/.config/fresh/themes. Refer to Fresh’s documentation for selecting a theme inside the editor.
FreshPage.note2: No elevated privileges are required. All operations target your home directory.

NvimPage.title: resources/
NvimPage.description: Complete Neovim configuration with essential plugins, LSP, DAP, formatting, linting, and custom themes with the X scheme.
NvimPage.requirementsDesc: Make sure you have all of these before installing:
NvimPage.installStep1: Clone this repository into your nvim config:
NvimPage.installStep2: Open Neovim. Lazy.nvim will automatically install all plugins on first start.
NvimPage.installStep3: (Optional) Run :Mason to check LSP server installation status.
NvimPage.themesDesc: All themes from references.md are available as colorschemes:
NvimPage.themesDefault: The default theme is x. Change it by adjusting vim.g.theme in init.lua.
NvimPage.keybindingsDesc: Shortcuts use the leader key and letters to avoid layout dependencies. You can change the leader in init.lua. To force keyboard mappings, define the following in init.lua:
NvimPage.pluginsUi: UI: lualine, bufferline, alpha, indent-blankline, colorizer
NvimPage.pluginsTools: Tools: telescope, trouble, todo-comments, conform, nvim-lint, oil, toggleterm, dap
NvimPage.note1: If a formatter or linter binary is not installed, conform and nvim-lint will skip it without failing. Use Mason or your preferred package manager to install them.

MacosPage.title: resources/
MacosPage.description: Lightweight macOS desktop environment: SketchyBar topbar and AeroSpace window manager, configured for productivity and visual clarity.
MacosPage.aboutSketchybar: SketchyBar — A customizable macOS topbar with workspace indicators, system stats, clock, volume, battery, and app launcher icons.
MacosPage.aboutAerospace: AeroSpace — A tiling window manager with virtual desktops (workspaces), keyboard-driven navigation, and automatic window placement rules.
MacosPage.structSketchybar: sketchybar/ — SketchyBar config: bar styles, items, plugins, colors, icons, and themes.
MacosPage.structAerospace: aerospace/ — AeroSpace config: workspace bindings, gaps, window rules, and keybindings.
MacosPage.structInstall: install.sh — Automated install script for dependencies and dotfiles.
MacosPage.structUninstall: uninstall.sh — Removes configs, services, and packages.
MacosPage.remoteDesc: Run directly from the repo without cloning:
MacosPage.remoteInstallCmd:
# Install
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xscriptor-colors/macos/main/install.sh | bash

# Or with wget
wget -qO- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xscriptor-colors/macos/main/install.sh | bash
MacosPage.manual1: Install Homebrew if not already installed.
MacosPage.manual3: Install Hack Nerd Font: brew install --cask font-hack-nerd-font.
MacosPage.manual6: Start services: brew services start sketchybar.
MacosPage.usageDesc: The most useful bindings, all using Ctrl as the primary modifier:
MacosPage.usageMoveWorkspace: Move window to workspace: Ctrl + Shift + number
MacosPage.usageApps: Open apps: Ctrl + Enter (Kitty), Ctrl + v (VS Code), Ctrl + b (Brave)
MacosPage.usageTopbar: Click workspace number on the topbar to switch
MacosPage.customDesc: SketchyBar supports multiple color palettes. Themes live in sketchybar/themes/ and use the same palette names as the VS Code Xscriptor themes: X, Madrid, Lahabana, Miami, Paris, Tokio, Oslo, Helsinki, Berlin, London, Praha, and Bogota.
MacosPage.customCmd:
# List the current theme and available palettes
./sketchybar/theme.sh

# Switch to a palette and reload the bar
./sketchybar/theme.sh miami
MacosPage.customNote: You can also cycle themes directly from the topbar: click the palette item to switch to the next palette. The active theme is persisted in ~/.config/sketchybar/theme (default: x).
